rules.text: Only active accounts with autopay switched on are drafted
Invoices BILD or DUE with money due on or before the horizon of N business days (default 3)
The autopay instrument must be ACTV, the account's own, and a bank mandate (sort code present)
An active PYMT hold stops drafting for the whole account
One live request per invoice: a CRTD SENT or SETL draft blocks another
Unapplied cash is netted off the account's invoices oldest first; nothing left = no draft
Draft date = invoice due date, never before the business date, rolled to a business day
All CRTD requests go to one file and become SENT under its file reference; trailer carries count and pence total

programs.purpose: Direct debit (ACH / BACS) draft generation. Phase 1 raises a payment request for every billed or due invoice of an autopay account that falls due within the draft horizon. Phase 2 writes every created request to the bank draft file in one unit of work and marks it SENT. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0200) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd 17-18 horizon in business days (default 03) 20-25 BACS service user number FILES : RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) DRAFTOUT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Returns file must prove: header, trailer count and pence total; otherwise nothing is returned or settled (RC 12)
Only R01 R02 R03 R04 are accepted
Only SENT or SETL drafts can be returned, and only once
Returned amount must equal the drafted amount
A settled draft that comes back has its receipt reversed NSF (BILPAYRC books the fee and the instrument failure)
A draft returned before settling records the instrument failure directly
R02/R03: the bank account is gone - the mandate is withdrawn now
A SENT draft with no return after the window (2 business days) settles as an ACH receipt dated the draft date
Each record is a savepoint; a failure backs out that record only and is reported

programs.purpose: Direct debit returns and settlement. Phase R works the bank's returns file: each returned draft becomes RTND, a settled draft's receipt is reversed NSF and the mandate failure recorded. Phase S settles every SENT draft that has passed the return window without a return: the money is receipted through BILPAYRC (source ACH) and the request becomes SETL. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0200) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd 17-18 return window in business days (default 2) FILES : RTNIN (I) RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Only billed (BILD) and due (DUE) items are aged; planned items are not yet receivable
Open amount = item - paid - written off; zero-open excluded
Bucket by days past due: due today or later is Current, then 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over 90
Credit (negative open) items fall into Current
Producer 0 is direct bill (no producer row)
Top 20 delinquent ranked by past due amount, ties by account no
Report and extract totals must agree or the run ends RC 12
Read-only report restarts from the beginning; checkpoint proves completion for the business date

programs.purpose: Receivables aging report. Ages the open amount of every invoiced item by days past due into Current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / 90+ buckets per account, with subtotals by producer within product, grand totals with bucket percentages, and the 20 most delinquent accounts. Writes the 132-column report and a CSV extract for finance. Read-only: no table is changed.

rules.text: Only ACTV producers flagged AGENCY_BILL_FLAG = Y
Statement holds BILD/DUE items on the producer's AB periods with an event date after the previous statement, up to business date
Net due to the carrier per item
Agency settles 30 days after the statement date
Nothing billed, nothing stated
One statement per producer per day; a rerun skips producers done

programs.purpose: Agency-bill statements. For every agency-bill producer, lists the items billed on its agency-bill (AB) policy periods since the last statement: gross, commission retained by the agency and net due to the carrier. Records the statement and writes it to the statement file. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0050) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) STMTOUT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Month end pays monthly and weekly producers; other runs weekly only
Only ACTV producers are paid
Pay EARN items not yet linked to a producer payment
Net earned below the plan PAY_THRESHOLD (or not positive) is carried forward
Items are linked first and the amount re-summed from the linked items, so the payment is exact
Paid by BACS to the producer mandate: COMMPAY, source COMM, ref = producer payment id
Payable balance reduced by the amount paid
Each producer is its own savepoint

programs.purpose: Producer payment run. Sums earned, unpaid commission items per producer, records a producer payment, links the items to it and raises a COMMPAY disbursement through BILDISB0. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0050) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Only PEND steps of OPEN processes with target date on or before the business date are executed, in process and step order
A step waits while an earlier step of its process is pending
When past due is at or below the plan threshold the process is exited (PAID) and its steps are skipped
Late fee is a one-time charge of plan LATE_FEE (pattern LATEFEE, instruction DELINQ); zero fee is completed without a charge
Late fee posts DR UNBILLED / CR FEEREV
CANCREQ asks GenApp operations to cancel for NONPAY as of the business date with the past due
After the write-off sweep a cleared process exits WRITEOFF
A failed step is rolled back and left PEND for the next run; later steps of the process are held

programs.purpose: Delinquency event executor. Works the pending BIL_DELINQ_EVENT steps of open processes whose target date has arrived, in process / step order: REMIND reminder document request LATEFEE late-fee charge, scheduled one-time NOI notice-of-intent document request CANCREQ CANCREQ event to GenApp operations WRITEOFF small-balance write-off sweep A process whose past due has already been cleared is exited (BILDLQSV DLQEXIT) instead.

rules.text: Only RQST requests dated on or before the business date go out
Recipient is the account's primary contact: company name for company contacts, else first and last name
A request without a primary contact address is marked ERRR
E-mail delivery needs an e-mail address on the primary contact
Invoice documents carry invoice number, amount due and due date; delinquency documents carry the policy number and past due
A request is written only after it is marked SENT from RQST
Trailer carries the record count, last document id and amount total for vendor reconciliation

programs.purpose: Document extract. Requested documents (status RQST) are resolved to their recipient and reference data and written to the fixed-length print-vendor file, then marked SENT. Requests that cannot be addressed are marked ERRR.

rules.text: Candidate has unapplied cash and no BILD/DUE item still open
No in-force period with future planned items (cash still needed)
Cash must have cleared: no receipt received in the last 10 days
Balances below the minimum refund stay on account
Payee is the primary payer; a company payer is paid by name
Autopay accounts are refunded by BACS to the autopay instrument; a rejected instrument falls back to cheque
Each account is a savepoint: a failed refund undoes only itself

programs.purpose: Overpayment sweep. Finds accounts holding unapplied cash that billing no longer needs and raises an OVERPAY refund to the primary payer through BILDISB0 DSBCRT. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0200) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd 17-23 minimum refund in pence (default 0000500) FILES : RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Only APPR disbursements due on or before the business date are sent
A DISB hold on the account keeps a BILL disbursement back (APPR)
BILL BACS needs an active instrument at send time
Sending clears the payable: DR DISBPAY / CR CASH
Claim payments raise DSBSENT to CLMS keyed on the claim check id
Cheque serials come from BILSEQGN CHQNO in disbursement id order
File holds exactly the rows sent by this run (run start timestamp) and trailer totals must agree

programs.purpose: Disbursement send. Phase 1 marks approved disbursements due by the business date SENT, clears DISBPAY to CASH in the ledger and tells ClaimsCore (DSBSENT) about claim payments. Phase 2 writes the bank bureau payments file (cheque / BACS) from the rows this run sent, so the file is always rebuilt whole on a restart. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0200) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) PAYFILE (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: EOD may only start from status O; B is set by one guarded UPDATE
Restart of BEGIN for the same business date is accepted (RC 4)
Every scheduled step must report; the latest record for a step wins
Stop at the first step with RC 8 or more (99 = abend) or missing; the date is not rolled and status stays B for operations
Next business date = one business day after the current date, over weekends and holidays (DTBUSD 1)
Date roll is one UPDATE guarded by status B and the old date so a rerun can never roll twice
Status and date changes are audited

programs.purpose: End-of-day driver, run twice by job BILEOD: MODE=BEGIN first step: BATCH_STATUS must be O (online day), set B (batch window). MODE=END last step: read the step-status file written by the job stream, record each step result in the audit trail, stop at the first step with RC >= 8, otherwise roll BUSINESS_DATE to the next business day (BILDATES DTBUSD), set PRIOR_BUS_DATE, LAST_EOD_TS and BATCH_STATUS O.

rules.text: Outbound CLMS events are delivered as NEW inbound rows in the claims queue, keyed by CLMSEQGN EVQ, then marked DONE
CANCREQ to GENA goes to the operations file (no GenApp API)
CLMPAYMT raises a CLMPAY disbursement, source CLMS, ref = check id, on the policy's billing account when one exists, else 0
A CLMPAYMT already disbursed (DSBDUP) is complete, not failed
DEDBILL bills a one-time DEDUCT charge on the in-force period, once per claim, DR UNBILLED / CR CLMPAY, then rebalances
POLISSUE retry needs an existing billing account for the customer
POLCHNG passes the full-term delta to PPCHG; zero delta is complete
Failed events stay claimed until the phase ends, then EVFAIL, so one bad event never blocks the queue for the rest of the run
Each event is a savepoint; a failure undoes only that event

programs.purpose: Billing event drainer (docs/EVENTS.md). Phase 1 delivers outbound events for ClaimsCore by inserting an inbound row into CLMDB.CLM_EVENT_QUEUE. Phase 2 writes CANCREQ events for GenApp to the operations work file. Phase 3 processes inbound events: CLMPAYMT (claim payment disbursement), DEDBILL (one-time deductible charge) and the POLISSUE / POLCHNG / POLCANC events BILGAPIN queued for retry. Events are claimed with BILEVTQ EVGET and closed with EVDONE or EVFAIL. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0100) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : CHKPT (O) OPSOUT (O) RPTOUT (O). The queue status is the restart point; failures held in PROC by an abended run are reclaimed by BILEVTQ after 30 minutes.

rules.text: Policies changed after the high- water mark, oldest change first
Life business is not billed here
Annual premium: motor = MOTOR premium; house = 0.30% of the rebuild value; commercial = sum of fire, crime, flood and weather premiums
Default plan MNTHLY10 for motor and house, QTRLY4 for commercial
New policy: billing account by GenApp customer, created from GENAPP.CUSTOMER when missing
Broker id is the producer code; an agency-bill producer makes the period agency billed (AB)
Known policy is re-priced only when premium differs and the period is not cancelled; change is effective on the GenApp change date, never before the period
Commits fall only on a change timestamp boundary and move the high-water mark with them
A rejected policy is queued as an inbound POL* event for retry

programs.purpose: GenApp policy intake. GenApp has no event queue, so this job reads GENAPP.POLICY rows changed since the high-water mark held in BIL_CONTROL 'GENAPPHW' (LAST_EOD_TS), derives the annual premium from the product detail table and raises the billing side directly: POLISSUE for a policy billing has never seen (account found or created from GENAPP.CUSTOMER, then BILPPER0 PPNEW) and POLCHNG when GenApp's premium differs from the billed premium (BILPPER0 PPCHG). A rejected policy is queued as an inbound POL event so the event drainer BILEVTDR retries it. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0100) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : CHKPT (O) RPTOUT (O). The high-water mark is the restart key: it is committed with the work, so a rerun simply resumes after it.

rules.text: Extract only while the day is closed to online (BATCH_STATUS B)
Product derived from the posting reference (item, distribution, write-off, charge, commission item, period); none is corporate cost centre CORP
T-account maps to a 6-digit GL account; unmapped lines go to GL suspense 199999 with RC 4
Gross DR and CR are extracted; net carries its own sign
Extract must balance (DR = CR) or the step ends RC 8
Trailer hash = sum of detail GL account numbers
A day with no ledger lines still sends header and trailer (RC 4)

programs.purpose: General-ledger extract for finance. Summarises the business date's ledger lines by T-account and product into the fixed GL interface file (header, one detail per GL account / cost centre, trailer with record count and DR, CR and account-number hash totals) and prints a control report. Read-only: nothing is marked as extracted; the file is rebuilt on every run.

rules.text: Only ACTV streams of ACTV accounts are invoiced
An active INVC hold skips the account for this run
One invoice per account + stream for PLAN items with event date on or before the business date
Prior balance (open BILD/DUE items) rides on the account's first invoice of the run
Due date = earliest item due date, never before the bill date
An account is all-or-nothing: any failure rolls back all of its invoices (savepoint)
Commits happen only on account boundaries, every COMMIT-FREQ invoices
A completed business date is not re-run unless forced

programs.purpose: Invoice run for the business date. Every invoice stream with PLAN items whose event date has arrived is billed: one invoice per account and stream, items moved to BILD, prior balance carried, ledger posted, invoice document requested and account balances refreshed.

rules.text: BILD items due on or before the business date with an open amount become DUE
Items and invoices already fully settled at due date close PAID
An invoice becomes DUE when its due date arrives with an open amount
Amount falling due posts DR DUE / CR BILLED
Account balances are refreshed after the transition (ACCTBAL)
Delinquency is considered only for items due before business date minus the plan GRACE_DAYS
Periods with an OPEN process are not re-evaluated
Each account / period is all-or- nothing (savepoint); commits on boundaries every COMMIT-FREQ

programs.purpose: Due transition for the business date. Phase 1 moves billed items and invoices that have reached their due date to DUE (or PAID when already settled), posts the amount falling due and refreshes account balances. Phase 2 starts delinquency (BILDLQSV DLQSTRT) for policy periods still past due once the delinquency plan's grace days have run out.

rules.text: One header first, one trailer last, details in between
Trailer count, amount total and cheque hash must equal the details or the whole file is rejected (RC 12)
A batch whose receipts are already on file is rejected unless this is a restart of that batch
Deposit date valid and not after the business date
A zero cheque cannot be receipted
Each cheque posts as method CHEQ, source LKBX, on the deposit date, referenced by cheque number
Each cheque is a savepoint: a failed receipt backs out alone
Posted + suspense + rejected must prove back to the trailer total

programs.purpose: Bank lockbox posting. Proves the lockbox file against its trailer (count, amount, cheque hash) and, only when the whole file balances, posts every cheque through BILPAYRC PAYRCV (source LKBX). Receipts that cannot be placed land in suspense; bad details are rejected and reported. PARM : 1-4 commit frequency (default 0200) 6-15 business date override yyyy-mm-dd FILES : LKBXIN (I) RESTART (I, optional) CHKPT (O) RPTOUT (O)

rules.text: Ledger proves to zero: total DR = total CR for the day and to date
Every transaction of the day must balance and carry ledger lines
Only chart-of-accounts T-accounts may carry ledger lines
Sub-ledger compared on the normal side: asset DR-CR, liability CR-DR
Item sub-ledgers by item status: PLAN = UNBILLED, BILD = BILLED, DUE = DUE (CLSD/CANC carry none)
Zero tolerance - a one-penny difference is a break (RC 8)
Stale account balance caches are warnings (RC 4), not breaks
Prior incomplete run is noted; rerun in full

programs.purpose: Ledger reconciliation. Builds the trial balance per T-account (DR - CR) for the business date and cumulative to date, proves the ledger nets to zero, lists transactions that do not balance or carry no lines, and reconciles each sub-ledger to its control T-account: UNBILLED / BILLED / DUE <- invoice items UNAPPLD <- account unapplied COMMPAY <- producer payable SUSPENSE <- open suspense Any break ends the step RC 8. Read-only.

rules.text: Entity, key and action are mandatory
Action is ADD, UPD, DEL or STAT
UPD needs a field name; STAT defaults the field to STATUS
An UPD/STAT whose before and after images are equal is not recorded (RC 04 AUDNOCHG)
ADD has no before image and DEL no after image; blank images are stored as NULL
Payment-instrument secrets (TOKEN_REF, SORT_CODE, EXPIRY_MMYY) are masked to their last four characters
Program defaults to the caller, user to BATCH
Audit keys come from sequence AUD

programs.purpose: Field-level audit trail. Records who changed which field of which entity, with before and after images, inside the caller's unit of work so the audit row commits or rolls back with the change it describes.

rules.text: The user checked defaults to the signed-on user
Limit type is WRITEOFF, DISBURSE, REVERSAL, PLANCHG or HOLDREL
Amount cannot be negative
Unknown or inactive users hold no authority
A role with no limit row for the type has no authority, even for a zero amount
An amount equal to the limit is within authority
Over limit: the supervisor chain is walked at most 5 levels for the first sufficient approver
Inactive supervisors cannot approve but the chain continues to their supervisor
A loop in the supervisor chain ends the search
Users never approve their own requests

programs.purpose: Authority limit check. Decides whether a user may perform a monetary or controlled action (write-off, disbursement, reversal, payment plan change, hold release) for an amount, from the user's role limit. When the amount is over the limit it walks the supervisor chain to name the first active approver whose role covers it.

rules.text: Code table and code are mandatory
Codes are matched in upper case
Only ACTIVE_FLAG = 'Y' codes are valid; retired codes return their description with RC 12
An unknown code table is reported separately from an unknown code
Found codes are cached for the run unit (50 entries, round robin); misses are never cached

programs.purpose: Validates a code against BIL_CODE_TABLE (the typelist store) and returns its description. Batch callers benefit from a small run-unit cache of codes already found.

rules.text: Dates are yyyy-mm-dd with numeric parts and '-' separators
Supported years 1900-2199; any result outside is rejected
Gregorian leap years: divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400
Blank date-1 / date-2 default to the business date (CA-BUS-DATE, else BIL_CONTROL 'SYSTEM ') except for DTVALD
Adding months keeps the day of month, clamped to the last day of a shorter target month
Business days exclude Saturday, Sunday and BIL_CALENDAR rows with HOLIDAY_FLAG = 'Y'
A business-day advance is limited to 0..250 days
Holidays are cached per run unit for the requested date window
Day of week is derived from day number 1 (1601-01-01) = Monday

programs.purpose: Date arithmetic for billing schedules, due dates, aging and delinquency timelines. All dates are ISO yyyy-mm-dd; arithmetic is done on integer day numbers (FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE / DATE-OF-INTEGER) so month and leap-year edges are exact.

rules.text: Logging never fails the caller: own errors are DISPLAYed and the request returns RC 04 at worst
Missing program / paragraph / user / tran are defaulted, never rejected
Severity: -911/-913 are retryable (W), other negative SQLCODEs and CICS RESPs are errors (E), the rest are informational (I)
Errors raised by BILSEQGN, or by a nested ERRLOG, go to SYSOUT only - the key generator cannot be re-entered to log itself
Error keys come from sequence ERR

programs.purpose: Central technical error logger. Writes one row to BIL_ERROR_LOG and a one-line message to SYSOUT (batch) / CEEMSG (CICS) so operations see the failure even when the caller's unit of work is rolled back. Never fails its caller.

rules.text: Only event types registered in EVENTS.md are accepted
Direction is I (inbound) or O (outbound) and must match the event type
Billing owns its queue: outbound events come from BILL, inbound events are addressed to BILL; source and target differ
Event key is mandatory and the payload must reach the start of the type's last field
An identical event still NEW or PROC is not queued twice (RC 04 EVDUPL returns the existing id)
EVGET serves the oldest NEW event first (CREATE_TS, EVENT_ID)
A claim flips NEW to PROC only if the row is still NEW; a lost race retries up to 5 times
PROC rows untouched for 30 minutes are reclaimed as a failed attempt before the next claim
Only PROC events can be marked DONE or FAILED
Each failure adds 1 to RETRY_COUNT; the fifth parks the event in ERRR
Event keys come from sequence EVQ

programs.purpose: Integration event queue for billing. Producers add events (EVPUT); the drainer BILEVTDR claims the oldest NEW event for a target and direction (EVGET), then marks it DONE or FAILED. Failed events are retried until the fifth failure parks them in ERRR for a trouble ticket. Event types and payload layouts: docs/EVENTS.md.

rules.text: Transaction type and reference type are mandatory
A transaction has 1 to 8 lines and at least one debit and one credit
Lines post only to the billing chart of T-accounts
Line side is D or C and the amount is greater than zero
Account-level T-accounts need an account id; commission T-accounts need a producer id
Total debits must equal total credits
Postings carry the business date, not the system clock
GLPOST may not set REVERSAL-OF; reversals go through GLREVS
A reversal mirrors the original lines with debit and credit swapped, on today's business date
A reversal cannot be reversed
A transaction can be reversed only once; the original is locked while the check is made
A reversal requested for an account must belong to it
Transaction keys come from sequence TXN

programs.purpose: Double-entry ledger posting. Every money movement in billing (charges, billing, cash, distribution, write-off, commission, disbursement) is recorded as one balanced BIL_TRANSACTION with 2..8 BIL_LEDGER_LINE rows against the billing T-accounts. Reversals post a mirror image linked to the original.

rules.text: A split has 1 to 24 parts
Down payment is 0 to 100 percent; 100 percent needs a single part
With a down payment, part 1 is the down payment and the balance is spread over parts 2..COUNT; without one the total is spread over all parts
Instalments are truncated to the penny; the rounding remainder is carried on part 1 so the parts always sum to the total
A non-zero total too small to give every instalment a penny is rejected
Negative totals (credits) split and rate symmetrically
Rates are basis points >= 0, rounded half away from zero
Pro-rata needs 0 <= DAYS-PART <= DAYS-WHOLE and DAYS-WHOLE > 0; a full period returns the total exactly
Arithmetic overflow is a validation error, never truncated

programs.purpose: Money arithmetic shared by billing: instalment splits, basis-point rates and day-based pro-rata so every program rounds the same way and splits always add back to the original amount.

rules.text: Block size 1..1000, default 1
Unknown sequence is an error, never auto-created
Exceeding MAX_VALUE wraps to 1 only when CYCLE_FLAG = 'Y'
Numbers are allocated by a single UPDATE so concurrent callers can never receive the same value

programs.purpose: Surrogate key and business number generator. Reserves a block of CA-SQ-COUNT values from a named sequence row and returns the first one, plus a formatted business number (prefix + zero-padded value) for numbering sequences such as ACTNO and INVNO.

rules.text: Account type; the payer type follows from it
Invoice day 1..28 (default 1) so every month has the day
Delinquency plan must exist and be active
PERS payer needs first and last name; COMM payer needs company
UK postcode format, stored as outward + space + inward
Account number from BILSEQGN ACTNO, never derived
One open account per GenApp customer (duplicate RC 16)
A GenApp customer number must exist in GENAPP.CUSTOMER
New account gets a primary payer (PAYR) and a monthly invoice stream anchored on invoice day
Account name defaults from the payer
Autopay needs an instrument, which cannot exist
Update/close need matching VERSION-NO (optimistic lock)
Field-level audit of name, invoice day, delivery, plan, autopay and payer address
Invoice day change re-anchors the active invoice stream
Autopay ON needs an active ACH or CARD instrument of this account
EMAL / BOTH delivery needs an e-mail address on the payer
Close only with no in-force period, zero balances, no open delinquency, no pending disb.
Close turns autopay off, closes streams, deactivates instruments
Balance buckets derived from open item amounts by invoice / due date; unapplied from receipts
Recompute keeps VERSION-NO; any drift from stored is audited

programs.purpose: Billing account service. Owns the account, its primary payer contact and its invoice stream, and is the only program that maintains the account balance buckets.

rules.text: Account number is required, 10 characters without blanks
Balances are recomputed from open items (ACCTBAL) on every inquiry; if that fails the stored buckets are shown with a warning
Net owed = unbilled + billed + due - unapplied
Collection status other than NORM and a closed account are flagged
Payer name: person = first + last name, company = company name
Policy periods page 4 at a time
Navigation carries an inquired account only
Service RC >= 90 rolls back the task (SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK)

programs.purpose: Account summary inquiry (transaction BACI, map BILACM). Looks the account up by number with BILACCT0 ACCTINQ, refreshes its balance buckets with ACCTBAL and shows status, collection status, balances, payer contact and the policy periods (4 per page, PF7/PF8). PF4 and PF5 carry the account to the invoice list and payment entry screens.

rules.text: Only PREMIUM pattern items earn commission
Producer is the requested one, else the period's; no producer = no commission (warning)
Commission is reserved only for an ACTV producer on an active commission plan
Rate = BIL_COMMISSION_RATE for plan/product/PREMIUM, else the plan DEFAULT_RATE_BPS
One live commission item per invoice item; cancelled items are never reserved
Reserve posts DR COMMRSV / CR COMMPAY; a chargeback the reverse
A chargeback on return premium (negative basis) is earned at once and reduces the payable
Earn basis P: commission earned = rate x amount paid on the item
EARN when earned reaches the commission or the item is fully settled; the rounding remainder is earned on that last payment
Earned commission is added to the producer PAYABLE_BALANCE
A payment reversal un-earns rate x reversed amount, capped at what was earned; state back to RSRV
Cancelled item: the whole commission is released (CANC), earned part taken off the payable
Commission already paid out is still recovered through the payable (may go negative)
Commission rows are updated only if unchanged since read

programs.purpose: Producer commission service. Reserves commission on premium invoice items for the period's producer, earns it as the insured pays, reverses earned commission when payments are reversed or items cancelled, and answers producer balance inquiries. Ledger model: COMMRSV is the commission expense reserved, COMMPAY the producer liability; the producer PAYABLE_BALANCE is the earned (payable) sub-ledger of COMMPAY.

rules.text: Reason must be OVERPAY CLMPAY COMMPAY or REFUND
Payee name is mandatory; cheques also need address and postcode
Reason fixes the source system: CLMPAY=CLMS COMMPAY=COMM OVERPAY/REFUND=BILL with account
SOURCE_SYSTEM + SOURCE_REF is unique among non-void rows
An active DISB hold blocks BILL-sourced disbursements
Account-funded disbursements cannot exceed UNAPPLIED_AMT and reduce it on create
Within DISBURSE authority -> APPR, otherwise PEND routed to approver
Ledger DR funding account (UNAPPLD CLMPAY COMMPAY) / CR DISBPAY
BACS for BILL source needs an active instrument on the account
Due date valid, not before the business date; defaults to it
Only PEND can be approved; the requester cannot approve own
Approver needs DISBURSE authority covering the amount
Only PEND or APPR can be voided and a void reason is required
Void reverses the create posting and restores account unapplied
Void of a COMMPAY reopens the producer payment: items back to EARN, payable balance restored
Receipt unapplied is consumed oldest first and restored newest first so ACCTBAL stays in step
COMMPAY source ref must be an existing producer payment; its producer owns the COMMPAY posting

programs.purpose: Outgoing money. Creates, approves, voids and inquires disbursements: account overpayment and refund cheques/BACS credits, claim payments raised by ClaimsCore and producer commission payments. Every create reserves the funding (account unapplied cash, claims or commission payable) against DISBPAY in the ledger; a void reverses that posting and restores the funding.

rules.text: Account and period are required; the period must belong to the account
Only an ACTV account and a period not yet closed can go delinquent
Plan defaults to the account's delinquency plan and must be active
Past due = open amount of DUE items of the period whose due date is before the business date
A process starts only when past due exceeds PASTDUE_THRESHOLD
An active DLNQ hold suppresses delinquency
At most one OPEN process per policy period
Step target = start date + days after start, rolled forward to a business day
A plan without steps cannot start a process
Collection status is DLNQ while any process is open and returns to NORM when the last one closes
Every status change is published to claims as a BILSTAT event
Exit reason PAID needs past due at or below threshold; other reasons close unconditionally
Closing a process cancels its pending event steps
Exit reasons are PAID WRITEOFF POLCANC MANUAL
BILSTAT status is DLNQ on start, CURR when cleared, PDUE when a residue below threshold remains

programs.purpose: Delinquency process service. Starts a delinquency process for a policy period whose past-due amount exceeds the plan threshold, lays out its dated event steps, exits processes once the past due is cleared and reports a process with its steps.

rules.text: Hold type is INVC, DLNQ, DISB or PYMT
Dates must be valid calendar dates; start defaults to the business date
No back-dated holds: start on or after the business date
End date is open (null) or on or after the start date
A reason is mandatory
Holds are placed only on an open account
One active hold per type per account: an ACTV
Release needs the HOLDREL authority row for the user role (BILAUTHZ, amount 0) - RC 20
Only an active hold can be released; release ends it on the business date
A hold applies when ACTV, started and not ended at the as-of date
Placing and releasing are audited

programs.purpose: Account holds. A hold suspends one kind of automatic processing on an account (invoicing, delinquency, disbursement, payment distribution) for a date range. Batch and online processes ask HLDCHK before acting on an account.

rules.text: Type is ACH, CARD, CHEQ or CASH
ACH and CARD need a vault token; CHEQ and CASH carry no token, card or bank details
Raw card / bank numbers are never accepted: an all-digit or short token is rejected
CARD needs last four and an expiry MMYY not before the business month
ACH needs a 6-digit sort code and the account's last four digits
Holder name on electronic instruments
Instruments are added only to an open account
A token is active at most once per account (RC 16)
Only an active instrument can be deactivated or fail (RC 24)
Withdrawing the autopay instrument turns autopay off through BILACCT0 (audited there)
Third failure deactivates the instrument (RC 04 INSDEACT)
Third failure raises a priority 2 trouble ticket due in two business days
Every instrument change audited

programs.purpose: Payment instrument service. Instruments are tokenised: only the vault token, last four digits, expiry and sort code are held. Tracks collection failures and withdraws an instrument (and account autopay) after repeated failures.

rules.text: Invoice is located by number when given, otherwise by surrogate id
Items list in due-date / install order; > 20 items is a warning
Account list is the newest 20 by bill date then invoice id
Ad-hoc invoicing only for an active (ACTV) account
An active INVC hold blocks ad-hoc invoicing
Cut-off defaults to business date and may not be more than 366 days ahead of it
One invoice per invoice stream, covering PLAN items with event date on or before the cut-off
Invoice due date is the earliest item due date, never before the bill date
Prior balance is the open amount of already billed (BILD/DUE) items, carried on the first invoice of the run only
Amount due = invoice amount + prior balance;
Billing posts DR BILLED / CR UNBILLED; a credit invoice posts the reverse
Every invoice raises a document request on the account's delivery method
Items are only billed if still PLAN; a count mismatch is a concurrent change (conflict)
Re-send not allowed for PLAN or CANC invoices
Re-send rejected while an earlier request is still RQST

programs.purpose: Invoice service. Inquiry of an invoice with its invoice items, list of an account's latest invoices, ad-hoc invoicing of planned items up to a cut-off date and re-send of an invoice document.

rules.text: A charge is scheduled once: it must be OPEN and have no items
Recurring positive charges need an in-force (INFC) period; one- time fees and credits may follow a cancelled period
LATEFEE REINSFEE CANCFEE or the one-time flag bill as one ONET item on the next invoice date
Next invoice date is the first stream anchor day on or after the business date
Down payment DPST: event date = charge date, due = event date + DAYS_BILL_BEFORE
Installments every M=1 Q=3 S=6 A=12 months, the first one FIRST_INST_MONTHS after period effective date
Installment due dates fall on the stream anchor day (clamped to the end of a short month)
Event date = due date minus DAYS_BILL_BEFORE, never before the business date
An installment due after period expiry merges into the previous item
An installment below the plan MIN_INST_AMOUNT merges into the previous item
Priority rank PREMIUM 1, TAX 2, all fees 5
INSTFEE is spread over installments 2..N only - no fee on the down payment
Mid-term charges (not NEWBIZ or RENEWAL) spread over the period's remaining planned premium due dates; none left = next invoice
A credit offsets unbilled items of the same pattern, latest due date first; any remainder is one CRED item on the next invoice
Reschedule preserves each charge's unbilled total exactly
Reschedule uses only the new plan's installment dates on or after the business date
The period's invoice stream must be ACTV with anchor day 1..31

programs.purpose: Invoice item scheduler. Splits a charge into invoice items following the policy period's payment plan and invoice stream (down payment, installments, one-time fees, credits spread over unbilled items) and reschedules the unbilled items of a period onto a new payment plan.

rules.text: Account number is required, 10 characters without blanks
12 invoices per page, newest first; PF7 / PF8 stop at the ends
Only the newest 20 invoices are returned by INVLST; the last page says so when the limit is hit
An invoice past its due date with an unpaid amount, not planned or cancelled, is shown as OVERDUE
Outstanding = account balance returned by INVLST
Service RC >= 90 rolls back the task (SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK)

programs.purpose: Invoice list (transaction BIVL, map BILIVM). Resolves the account number with BILACCT0 ACCTINQ, lists the account's newest invoices with BILINVSV INVLST, 12 rows a page with PF7/PF8, flags overdue invoices and shows the outstanding balance. PF5 carries the account to payment entry.

rules.text: Only the three listed options exist
PF1 / PF2 / PF4 are shortcuts for options 1 / 2 / 3
An account number, when keyed, is 10 characters with no embedded blanks
Invoice list (3) needs an account number
PF3 or CLEAR on the menu ends the BillingCore session

programs.purpose: BillingCore main menu (transaction BMNU, map BILMNU). Routes by option or PF key with XCTL to the account summary (BILACIP / BACI), payment entry (BILPAYP / BPAY) and invoice list (BILIVMP / BIVL), carrying the account number.

rules.text: Receipt must exist, belong to the account, and be RCVD or APPL
Amount defaults to the receipt's unapplied money, never above it
Target invoice must belong to the account; its items go first
Pass 1 past-due (DUE) items, oldest due date first
Pass 2 billed-not-due (BILD) items, oldest due date first
Pass 3 planned items in mode A only, earliest event date first
Within a date premium before tax before fees (PRIORITY_RANK)
Partial payment: an item takes the lesser of its outstanding and the money left; settled -> CLSD
Invoice AMOUNT_DUE follows its items; nothing due -> PAID
PREMIUM-pattern items earn commission on the amount applied
One balanced ledger entry per batch: UNAPPLD against DUE, BILLED or UNBILLED by the item's balance bucket
Undistributed remainder stays unapplied on receipt and account
Undo never deletes: it writes a negative mirror row per original
Restored item status comes from invoice link and due date
Earned commission follows the money back out
Item, receipt and account updates are guarded against concurrent change (STALEVER)

programs.purpose: Payment distribution engine. Spreads the unapplied money of one receipt across the open invoice items of its account in the carrier's standard order, books the distribution to the ledger and keeps receipt, item, invoice, account and commission balances in step. DSTUNDO backs a receipt's distributions out with mirror rows.

rules.text: An account or an invoice number is required; when both are keyed the invoice must be the account's
Amount: digits, optional commas, at most 2 decimals, above zero
Online receipts are limited to 250,000.00; larger go to treasury
Method must be an active PAYMTHD code
A reference is required for every method except CASH
Received date, when keyed, must be a valid date (blank = business date)
Posting needs a validated screen (PF5 only in the confirm step)
A posted screen cannot be posted again (double-post guard)
Paying more than is owed is allowed but warned (stays unapplied)
Service RC >= 90 rolls back the task (SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK)

programs.purpose: Payment entry (transaction BPAY, map BILPYM). Two-step: ENTER validates the receipt (account or invoice number, amount, method, reference, received date), shows the payer and what is owed and protects the fields; PF5 then posts it through BILPAYRC PAYRCV and shows the money id, the amount distributed to items and the amount left unapplied. PF12 returns to amend.

rules.text: Receipt amount must be above zero
Method (PAYMTHD) and source (RCPTSRC) must be active codes
Received date valid and not after the business date
Account resolved by id, then by account number, then by invoice
An invoice on another account is not targeted; money follows the account number
Unresolved money -> suspense NOACCT; closed account ACCTCLSD
Same account, reference, amount and date already live = duplicate
The paying instrument must be the account's own
Receipt books DR CASH and CR UNAPPLD (SUSPENSE when unplaced)
Active PYMT hold keeps the money unapplied on the account
Due items only (mode D), target invoice first
Clearing all past due exits open delinquency processes
Reversal reasons NSF WRONGACC REFUND STOPPYMT
Reversal above the user's REVERSAL limit is refused (RC 20)
Reversal undoes distributions, then reverses the cash entry
NSF fee only while code table NSFFEE has an active row; billed as a one-time charge
NSF and stopped payment count as an instrument failure
Only OPEN suspense matches, and only to an active account
A reversed receipt is final

programs.purpose: Payment receipt service. Records money received from any channel, finds the billing account it belongs to, books it to cash and hands it to the distribution engine; money that cannot be placed goes to suspense. Also reverses receipts (NSF, wrong account, refund, stopped payment), answers receipt enquiries and matches suspense items to an account.

rules.text: A new period needs an existing, active (ACTV) account
Product is M, H, C or E; billing method DB (direct) or AB (agency)
Expiry after effective date and the term at most 18 months
Payment plan must exist and be active
Producer resolved from the GenApp broker id must be ACTV; agency bill needs an agency-bill producer
Term = previous term + 1 for the policy: first term NEWBIZ, later RENEWAL; no overlap with a prior term that is not cancelled
Period bills on the account's active stream of the plan's frequency, else its first active stream
Insurance Premium Tax is 12% of premium, charged as TAX
Installment fee = plan fee x (installments - 1)
Charges post DR UNBILLED / CR PREMREV (premium) and CR FEEREV (tax, fees); credits the reverse
Commission is reserved on every premium item of a producer-sold period and released on items that are cancelled
Mid-term change: the full-term delta is pro-rated from the change date to expiry (POLCHG)
Change and cancel dates fall within the period
Cancel only from INFC with a valid CANCRSN reason; unearned premium and its tax are returned pro rata as CANCEL credits
Planned installments wholly offset by the credit are cancelled and their installment fees waived
An account left in credit by a cancellation is flagged (RC 04 ACCTCRED) for the batch unapplied / disbursement path
Reinstatement only from CANC within 30 days of the cancel date: cancel credits reversed (REINST) plus the delinquency plan REINSFEE
Plan change only for INFC to a different active plan, within PLANCHG authority for the unbilled amount, audited
Period updates are guarded by VERSION_NO
A period is found by PP-ID, else policy number + term (latest term when the term is zero)

programs.purpose: Policy period and billing instruction service. Creates new-business and renewal periods with their premium, tax and installment-fee charges, bills mid-term changes pro rata, cancels with a pro-rata return-premium credit, reinstates, changes the payment plan and returns a period with its invoice item schedule.

rules.text: Producer code is the GenApp broker id: positive and unique (duplicate RC 16)
Producer name is required
Tier is STD, GOLD or PLAT (default STD)
Commission plan must exist and be active
Pay cycle M monthly or Q quarterly; agency bill Y or N
New producers start ACTV with a zero payable balance
The GenApp broker link is immutable
Status moves ACTV <-> SUSP and ACTV/SUSP -> TERM; TERM is final
Suspending or terminating a producer with a payable balance above zero is rejected (RC 24)
Agency bill cannot be switched while agency statements are open
Payable balance is maintained by commission processing only
Commission plan change and every other field change is audited

programs.purpose: Producer (broker) maintenance. A producer is the billing view of a GenApp broker: PRODUCER-CODE holds the GenApp BROKERID. Carries the commission plan, tier, payment cycle and agency bill flag used by commission processing.

rules.text: Write-off reason must be an active WOREASON code; a sweep defaults to SMALLBAL
Only billed items (BILD / DUE) with a positive open amount can be written off
Amount must not exceed the open amount; zero means all of it
Over the user's WRITEOFF limit the write-off is held PEND for the approver with no financial effect
One pending write-off per item
A pending write-off is approved by someone other than the requester, within their limit, while the item still has the open amount
Ledger DR WRITEOFF / CR DUE (CR BILLED while not yet due)
Item is CLSD once paid plus written off covers its amount
Sweep takes billed items past their due date whose open amount is below the delinquency plan WRITEOFF_THRESHOLD
Reversal needs REVERSAL authority and an approved, unreversed write-off; a PEND one is simply cancelled
Reversal reopens a CLSD item as DUE when past due, else BILD
Reversal posts the mirror entry (GLREVS) of the original posting
Items are updated only if paid, written-off and status are unchanged since read
Account balances are recomputed after every financial change

programs.purpose: Write-off service. Writes off the open amount of one billed invoice item, sweeps an account's small past-due balances below its delinquency plan threshold, approves write-offs that were held for a higher authority, and reverses or cancels write-offs.

rules.text: Only ACTIVE catastrophes already started on the business date with a valid window are applied
Loss date inside the window, both ends inclusive
Postcode area match is the area letters followed by a digit, so area B never takes BS postcodes
Only OPEN claims with a blank CAT code; an existing tag is never overwritten
Tag under optimistic lock; a stale claim is left for next run
Tagged claims are re-segmented (CLMSEGMT stores the result) and segment / severity moves reported

programs.purpose: Catastrophe tagging. For every active declared catastrophe, OPEN claims with no CAT code whose loss date falls in the event window and whose loss postcode is in the event postcode area are tagged, written to history and re-segmented (CLMSEGMT). Counts and incurred are reported per catastrophe. FILES : CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMCATCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMCATCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : at CT-CAT-CODE after CT-LAST-CLAIM-ID

rules.text: A check needs at least one payment txn and every txn on it must be SUBM, else it is held
Check amount must equal the sum of its payment txns and be > 0
Payee name required; a cheque needs payee address and postcode
Payee with sanction status HIT is never paid (held for compliance)
Check number from CHKNO, issue date = business date, update guarded on status PEND
Only CHEQ pay method goes to the bank positive-pay file
Every issued check raises CLMPAYMT to billing
Bank sort code and account on the control card must be numeric

programs.purpose: Claim check issuance. Every PEND check due on or before the business date whose payment transactions are all SUBM is numbered (CHKNO), set ISSU with the issue date, sent to billing as a CLMPAYMT event and, for cheques, written to the bank positive-pay file. Checks that cannot be issued are held and reported with a reason. FILES : POSPAY - positive-pay issue file (CLMCHKPP 150) CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMCHKCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMCHKCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : after CK-LAST-CHECK-ID; positive-pay details are buffered and written only after each commit so the bank never sees an uncommitted check number.

rules.text: Match basis: same policy, else same insured (customer) on a different policy, else same vehicle registration on an incident
Same loss type and loss dates no more than 7 days apart
Similar cause: identical cause or the same cause family (CLMDUPCF)
Later = reported later (claim id breaks a tie); only the later claim is flagged, and only while OPEN and not already suspected
Flagging bumps VERSION_NO and is guarded on the flag still N
A flagged claim is re-scored by SIU so the duplicate weighs in the referral decision

programs.purpose: Duplicate claim detection across the book. Pairs an OPEN, not yet suspected claim with any earlier claim on the same policy, the same insured or the same vehicle registration, of the same loss type, with loss dates within 7 days and a similar cause. The later claim is flagged DUP_SUSPECT_FLAG, written to history and re- scored by SIU; every pair is reported. FILES : CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMDUPCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMDUPCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : later-claim ids above DK-LAST-CLAIM-ID; commits only fall between later claims

rules.text: A date the scheduler did not ask for is never closed: already rolled is RC 4 (no-op), behind is RC 12
EOD starts only from batch status O (open) or H (held); E means an EOD is already running
The day cannot close until the GL extract for it has completed - status H and RC 12
Stuck or errored events, unissued due checks and unsealed audit rows are warnings (RC 4)
Next date = next calendar day rolled forward to a business day
The roll is one optimistic UPDATE on the expected date in status E

programs.purpose: End-of-day driver for CLM_CONTROL. Last step of the nightly stream (CLMEOD): checks the day is ready to close, prints the day's statistics and rolls the claims business date to the next business day. PARM: optional yyyy-mm-dd = business date the scheduler expects to close (restart guard).

rules.text: Escalate OPEN activities whose escalation date has passed and that are not already escalated
New owner is the user's supervisor, else the group supervisor; must be active and not the owner, else flag in place
Escalated work goes to priority 1. Guarded on
Overdue = OPEN with due date before the business date; users at or over the alert level are flagged to team leaders
Aged claim = OPEN, opened before the window, no activity created or completed inside it and no open review already
Aged claim with nil reserves gets CLOSEREV, otherwise RSVREV

programs.purpose: Nightly activity escalation sweep. 1. OPEN activities past their escalation date and not yet escalated are flagged, raised to priority 1 and reassigned to the owner's supervisor, with a claim history row. 2. Overdue (past due date) open activities are counted per user for the workload report. 3. OPEN claims with no activity created or completed in the aged window get a CLOSEREV or RSVREV review activity. FILES : CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMESCCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMESCCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : phase E after EK-LAST-KEY (activity id), phase A after EK-LAST-KEY (claim id)

rules.text: Only events created before the run started are drained
Outbound type must be in the catalogue and its payload must pass the EVENTS.md layout check
Delivery is idempotent: an equal inbound row already on the BIL queue completes the event
Delivered row is direction I, source CLMS, status NEW, keyed from the billing EVQ sequence
BILSTAT refreshes the cached billing status on every non- closed claim of the policy
DLNQ / CANC is a coverage concern: history row on each open claim
BILLCHK activity only when the pattern exists and the claim has no open BILLCHK activity
DSBSENT clears PEND/ISSU checks; CLRD is a duplicate, HOLD (still awaiting approval) and VOID fail
An existing issue date is kept, otherwise the billing sent date
A failed event is rolled back to its savepoint and EVFAILed; an event reaching ERRR gives RC 8

programs.purpose: Integration event drainer for CLM_EVENT_QUEUE. Phase OUTB delivers outbound claims events for target BILL (CLMPAYMT, DEDBILL) by inserting an inbound row into BILDB.BIL_EVENT_QUEUE, then marks the claims row DONE through CLMEVTQ. Phase INBD processes inbound BillingCore events (BILSTAT, DSBSENT) against claims data. PARM: OUT | IN | ALL (default ALL), optional ',nnnn' commit frequency.

rules.text: Feed must balance (header first, trailer last, count and damage hash) or nothing is staged
A source + external reference already DONE is a replay: reject
Loss date valid, not after the business date, not over 3 years old
Motor losses need a vehicle reg on the policy schedule; injury flag must be Y or N; cause must belong to the loss type (LOSSCAUS)

First exposure from loss type, cause and injury flag: AUTO VEHDAMAG on COLL (impact causes) or COMP; PROP theft CONTENTS, other PROPDAMA on DWELLING/BLDG; LIAB PROPDAMA on LIAB_PD; injury BODINJUR on LIAB_BI for the reporter as injured pers
Initial reserve from the table by exposure type and severity; a higher reporter estimate is used up to 3x table and coverage limit
Intake is atomic: any failure after CLMNEW rolls back to the claim savepoint, intake ERRR
Reserve above batch authority is recorded pending approval (PAPR); intake DONE with RSVAPRV warning
Reject rate above the control card tolerance fails the run
Intake source must be a bulk HOWRPTD channel: WEB APP BRKR AGGR

programs.purpose: Bulk first notice of loss intake from the web and partner portal gateway. Balances the feed, stages every FN record into CLM_FNOL_INTAKE, then works the NEW intake rows: validate, open the claim (CLMNEW), first incident (INCNEW), first exposure (EXPNEW) and the initial reserve (RSVSET) as one unit of work per claim. FILES : FNOLIN - intake feed (CLMFNLIN, 600 F) FNOLREJ - rejected intake images (CLMFNLRJ, 700) CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMFNLCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMFNLCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : phase S restarts staging after CK-INPUT-COUNT feed records; phase P restarts after CK-LAST-INTAKE-ID. Commit per claim.

rules.text: The day's financials are posted (SUBM) transactions dated on the business date plus older PAPR ones approved to SUBM on it
GL accounts come from the posting table by transaction type and cost type; an unmapped pair posts to suspense with RC 4
A negative amount (reserve take- down, void) swaps debit / credit
Policy type is the cost centre
Journal must balance; otherwise RC 12 and the date is not marked extracted
One extract per business date unless PARM RERUN or the previous run for the date did not finish

programs.purpose: Claims financial extract for the general ledger. Summarises the business day's submitted and approved claim transactions by policy type, cost type and transaction type into one balanced GL journal (paid loss, paid ALAE, case reserve change, recoveries, recovery reserve change) with header and trailer hash totals. PARM: optional 'RERUN' to re-extract a date.

rules.text: Every non-draft claim without an ISO request is queued once (INIT)
Parties added or changed after the last SENT request re-queue the claim (UPDT) unless a request is already pending
A request needs claim number, loss date and insured name; motor also a vehicle registration - an incomplete request stays PEND
Party list capped at WS-MAX-PARTIES
Responses post only if the file has a header and the trailer count balances the detail records
Only SENT requests accept a response; RCVD is a duplicate and a claim number mismatch rejects
A bureau-rejected request (ER) is reset to PEND for resubmission
Two or more matches trigger SIU scoring and a claim history row

programs.purpose: ISO ClaimSearch-style industry fraud bureau interface. PARM SEND: queue CLM_ISO_REQUEST rows for new claims (INIT) and claims whose parties changed since the last submission (UPDT), then write every PEND request with its parties to ISOOUT and mark it SENT. PARM RECV: balance the ISOIN response file, post match counts (RCVD) and refer claims with two or more bureau matches to SIU scoring. Optional ',nnnn' after the mode = commit freq.

rules.text: Open claims in segment / adjuster sequence
Age is days from the reported date to the business date
Incurred = reserves + paid - recovered; a stored total that disagrees is flagged (RC 4)
Closed this month = close date from the first of the business month to the business date
Days open run from the open date (reported date if never opened) to the close date
DUPLICAT closures are counted by reason but kept out of the average days-to-close

programs.purpose: Loss run and aging report. Section 1 lists every open claim by segment and adjuster with its age bucket (days since reported), reserves, paid and incurred, with adjuster, segment and grand totals by bucket. Section 2 lists claims closed this month with days open and final financials. Every open claim is also written to a CSV extract for the claims MI team. PARM: optional commit frequency (nnnn).

rules.text: A claim is re-ceded when it has a financial transaction dated the business date
Treaties attach by policy type with the loss date inside the treaty period
QS ceded = incurred x CEDED_PCT, nil when incurred is not positive, capped at the treaty limit
XOL ceded = incurred - retention, floor nil, capped at the limit
No movement (gross and ceded unchanged) writes no bordereau
First time ceded reaches 50,000 the cession is flagged notified and a large-loss notice raised
An XOL cession row is created only once the layer is pierced
Unknown treaty type or XOL with no limit is skipped and reported

programs.purpose: Reinsurance cession. For every claim whose incurred moved today (a financial transaction on the business date) the treaties in force for its policy type at the loss date are applied: quota share cedes a percentage, excess of loss cedes the layer above retention up to the limit. CLM_RI_CESSION is upserted, first large-loss crossings are flagged for notice and every movement goes to the bordereau file. FILES : BORDX - cession bordereau (CLMRIRBD, 200) CHKPT - checkpoint / restart (CLMRIRCK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMRIRCC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : after RK-LAST-CLAIM-ID; bordereau lines are buffered and written after each commit

rules.text: Benchmark by exposure type and claim severity (1-5, clamped); '*' row for unlisted types
Under-reserved when the open reserve is below 80% of the benchmark still to be paid
Stale when the reserve is open and unchanged for 90 days or more
Velocity: reserve would be used up within 30 days at the average payment rate since creation
Exposure open over 30 days with no reserve and no payment
One open RSVREV activity per exposure - never duplicated

programs.purpose: Reserve adequacy review. For every open exposure compares the open reserve with a benchmark by exposure type and claim severity, checks how long the reserve has gone unchanged and how fast it is being paid down, and raises an RSVREV activity for the adjuster on each flagged exposure. PARM: optional commit frequency (nnnn).

rules.text: Verification always resumes after the last sealed row; sealed rows are never re-walked
The run seals up to the head captured at start; rows appended during the run wait for tomorrow
Each verified slice is committed before the next is walked
Every row up to the verified head must end the run sealed
The verified head hash must equal the stored CHAIN_HASH of that row
A broken link prints its sequence and fails the run (RC 12); rows before it stay sealed

programs.purpose: Nightly audit chain seal. Calls CLMAUDCH AUCVFY from the last sealed row (FROM-SEQ 0) in slices until the chain head captured at start is proven; CLMAUDCH seals each proven row and this program commits per slice, confirms every row up to the verified head is sealed, cross-checks the head hash against the table and records the head in the seal register. A broken link is printed with its sequence and ends the run RC 12. FILES : SEALREG - seal register (CLMSEARG, 120) CHKPT - checkpoint trail (CLMSEACK, 80) SYSIN - control card (CLMSEACC, 80) RPTOUT - run report (132) RESTART : inherent - the last sealed row is the restart key; CHKPT is reconciled against it on restart

rules.text: Event code and payload required; claim id 0 means a system event
Appends are serialised by locking CLM_SEQUENCE 'AUC' before the chain tail is read
Genesis links to sixteen zeros
DIGEST = FNV-1a-64 of the full 400-byte payload as passed
CHAIN_HASH = FNV-1a-64 of the 32 characters PREV_HASH || DIGEST
Never extend a chain whose tail fails its own hash check
Chain sequence is contiguous: the new row is tail + 1
AUCVFY FROM-SEQ 0 resumes after the last sealed row; FROM-SEQ n anchors on row n-1's hash
A link breaks on a sequence gap, PREV_HASH mismatch, CHAIN_HASH mismatch or malformed hex; the first break is reported
At most 50000 rows per AUCVFY call; a partial walk is RC 04
Rows proven intact are sealed; nothing is sealed past a break
A broken chain is logged to CLM_ERROR_LOG as a security event

programs.purpose: Tamper-evident audit hash chain for regulated claim events (reserve and payment authority, SIU referral, litigation, close/reopen). Each row stores a digest of the caller's 400-byte payload and a chain hash over the previous row's hash and that digest, so altering, removing or re-ordering any committed row breaks every link after it.

rules.text: Table and code are mandatory
An unknown code is not found
Retired codes stay on file for history but may
A child code must carry the given parent code, or '*' (valid under every parent)
The parent code must itself be an active code of the parent table (LOSSCAUS -> LOSSTYPE, COSTCAT -> COSTTYPE)

programs.purpose: Code table validation against CLM_CODE_TABLE (ClaimCenter typelists). Returns the description of an active code, and for dependent typelists (loss cause within loss type) checks that the code belongs to the given parent code.

rules.text: Dates are ISO yyyy-mm-dd with hyphens in positions 5 and 8
Supported years 1601..9999
Gregorian leap year: divisible by 4, not by 100 unless by 400
A blank input date defaults to the business date (CA-BUS-DATE, else CLM_CONTROL 'SYSTEM')
Adding months clamps the day to the target month end; month-end is not sticky
Month offsets limited to +/-1200 (100 years)
Signed difference DATE-2 minus DATE-1; a blank
Day number 1 (1601-01-01) was a Monday, so
Saturdays, Sundays and active HOLIDAY code rows are not business days
DTBUSD rolls DATE-1 forward to the first business day on or after it (NUMBER is ignored)
More than 31 consecutive non- business days means the holiday table is corrupt - request fails
Holidays are cached per year for the run unit; malformed HOLIDAY rows are ignored with a warning
A result outside 1601..9999 is a validation error
DTVALD reports an invalid date as RC 04 with CA-DT-VALID = 'N'

programs.purpose: Date arithmetic on ISO yyyy-mm-dd dates. All claims date maths (activity due dates, reserve review cycles, late-reporting checks, payment scheduling) is routed through this program so weekend / UK bank holiday handling and month-end rules live in exactly one place.

rules.text: The logger always returns to the caller; RC is 00, or 04 when the row could not be written
Every error is DISPLAYed before any Db2 access
Errors raised by CLMSEQGN are DISPLAY-only (no recursive CALL)
Missing program, text or user are defaulted, never rejected
A failing insert is DISPLAYed and swallowed

programs.purpose: Central technical error logger. Writes one row to CLM_ERROR_LOG (key from sequence ERR) and a DISPLAY line (SYSOUT in batch, CSSL/job log under CICS) so the error is traceable even when the caller's unit of work is later rolled back. The logger never fails its caller.

rules.text: Only event types registered in EVENTS.md
Direction, source and target come from the registry; supplied values must agree with it
Key is mandatory and must equal the key field that leads the payload
Payload at least the registered layout length; amount fields are 13 digits plus a trailing sign
Duplicates suppressed: one event per key for CLMPAYMT / DSBSENT, identical payload for DEDBILL
BILSTAT coalesces: a newer status overwrites an unprocessed one
FIFO candidates for EVGET (expired leases too)
Events of one type and key are serialised: none is issued while another holds a live lease
Claiming is optimistic; a lost race moves on to the next row
PROC lease is 30 minutes; an expired lease is re-issued and counts as a retry
Only an event this drainer holds (PROC) is done
After 5 retries the event is parked in ERRR and logged for an operations activity

programs.purpose: Integration event queue (CLM_EVENT_QUEUE) API per docs/EVENTS.md. Producers EVPUT outbound events for BillingCore (CLMPAYMT, DEDBILL); the drainer CLMEVTDR takes work with EVGET and finishes it with EVDONE or EVFAIL.

rules.text: Claim id, event type and description are mandatory
History is only written for an existing claim
User defaults to SYSTEM, program to the calling program
Low-values in descriptions are replaced by spaces
An identical entry (claim, event, user, text) within 60 seconds is suppressed with RC 04
History is append-only: no update or delete request exists
Lists are newest first, at most 20 rows; RC 04 HISMORE when older rows exist

programs.purpose: Claim history writer and reader. Every business service records what it did to a claim here (ClaimCenter "History" tab); screens list the newest entries.

rules.text: Split count 1..24
Down-payment percent 0..100
Regular parts are truncated to the penny; the rounding remainder is carried on the first part
Control total: the parts must add back to TOTAL
Rounding is half away from zero, so a charge and its reversal mirror exactly
RESULT = TOTAL * RATE-BPS / 10000 (rounded)
Pro-rata needs DAYS-WHOLE > 0 and 0 <= DAYS-PART <= DAYS-WHOLE
PART(1) = RESULT, PART(2) = TOTAL - RESULT, so a
Arithmetic overflow is rejected, never truncated silently

programs.purpose: Money arithmetic in GBP pence precision. One home for splits, percentage (basis point) rates and pro-rata apportionment so every caller rounds the same way: structured settlement instalments, reinsurance cessions, liability apportionment, deductible and VAT calculations.

rules.text: Block size 1..1000, default 1
Unknown sequence is an error, never auto-created
Exceeding MAX_VALUE wraps to 1 only when CYCLE_FLAG = 'Y'
Numbers are allocated by a single UPDATE so concurrent callers can never receive the same value
A non-cyclic sequence past 90% of MAX_VALUE still allocates but returns warning SEQHIGH
Sequence names are upper-case alphanumeric

programs.purpose: Surrogate key and business number generator for the claims application. Reserves a block of CA-SQ-COUNT values from a named CLM_SEQUENCE row and returns the first one, plus a formatted business number (prefix + zero-padded value) for numbering sequences such as CLMNO and CHKNO.

rules.text: Selection is C, S or V
One V at a time and not mixed with C / S
View opens claim inquiry for the V row, else the cursor row
Only OPEN activities can be completed or skipped
Service RC >= 90 backs out every selection of the request
Escalated rows are highlighted
Overdue = due date before today
ACTLST returns the 20 most urgent; a full list is flagged

programs.purpose: "My activities" for the signed-on user (CLMACTV0 ACTLST, user from EXEC CICS ASSIGN). Select C to complete (ACTCMP), S to skip (ACTSKP), V to view the claim; ENTER processes the selections and refreshes the list. PF4 views the claim of the V row or the cursor row (XCTL CLMINQP); PF7/PF8 page; PF5 refresh; PF3 menu.

rules.text: Activities cannot be raised on a closed claim
Pattern loss type must be the claim loss type or '*'
Due date = business date plus TARGET_DAYS business days
Escalation date = due date plus ESCALATION_DAYS business days
Assignee defaults to the claim owner, else the requesting user; assignee must be an active user
Exposure must belong to the claim and must not be closed
Generation skips a pattern that already has an OPEN activity on the same claim and exposure
Only the assignee or the assignee's supervisor may complete or skip an activity
Approval activities stay open while their transaction is PAPR
Mandatory activities cannot be skipped
Only OPEN activities can be completed or skipped
User queue lists OPEN activities by due date then priority; claim list shows OPEN first
Approval transaction must belong to the same claim

programs.purpose: Claim activity (diary) engine. Creates single activities from an activity pattern, generates every pattern bound to a workflow trigger event, completes and skips activities under assignee / supervisor authority and lists work queues.

rules.text: Rules are evaluated in RULE_SEQ order; '*' matches any value and severity must reach MIN_SEVERITY
Region = REGION code-table entry for the loss postcode area (first 2 chars, 1 when the 2nd is a digit); unknown -> UNKN
Eligible adjuster: active, below MAX_CLAIMS, LOB_SKILLS holds the policy type
RRBN picks the adjuster assigned longest ago; LOAD picks fewest open claims (then longest ago)
A matched rule whose group is inactive or has no eligible adjuster falls through to the next rule
Nobody eligible: the FNOL supervisor triages
OPEN_CLAIMS moves with the claim owner; LAST_ASSIGN_TS stamped on every new assignment
Exposures inherit the claim owner unless bodily injury or litigated (routed via the LIAB rules)
Transfer target must be active, hold the LOB skill and sit in a group of the same LOB
Transfer over capacity is allowed with warning OVERCAP
On a change of owner, inherited exposures and the old owner's open activities move too
Closed claims/exposures cannot be assigned
Specialist LIT / SIU groups may receive a claim of any LOB

programs.purpose: Assignment engine. Chooses the handling group from CLM_ASSIGN_RULE (loss type, segment, severity, region) and the adjuster inside it by round robin or load balancing, assigns exposures and performs manual transfers, while keeping adjuster workload counters current.

rules.text: Limit types are RSVEXP PAYEXP PAYCLM INCCLM only
Claim-level limit types (PAYCLM, INCCLM) ignore coverage type and use the '*' row
A coverage-specific limit row overrides the '*' default row
No row at all means zero authority
An inactive user has no authority
Amount within limit when AMOUNT <= LIMIT (limit is inclusive)
Approver search climbs at most 5 supervisor levels
Inactive supervisors are skipped but still count as a level
A supervisor loop (user already seen in the chain) stops the walk
No approver found is a warning (RC 04 NOAPPRVR), not an error

programs.purpose: Financial authority limits. Resolves the user's authority profile from CLM_USER, reads the limit for the limit type and coverage type (falling back to the '' default row) and says whether AMOUNT is within it. When it is not, walks the supervisor chain (CLM_USER.SUPERVISOR_ID, at most 5 levels) and returns the first supervisor whose own limit covers AMOUNT as the APPROVER.

rules.text: Loss date valid, not after the business date, not before 1990; reported date >= loss date
Loss type and cause from code tables; cause must be a child of the loss type
Loss description required, at least 10 characters
Unverified (not found) policy is accepted with COVERAGE_IN_QSTN Y
Loss outside the policy period is rejected unless override 'O' (or 'Y') is passed
Policy type must agree with loss type: M AUTO, H PROP, C PROP/LIAB
Adverse billing or unverifiable cover puts coverage in question
Duplicate suspect: same policy, same cause, loss date +/- 3 days
Catastrophe tag when the loss postcode area/district and date fall in an active CLM_CATASTROPHE
Reporter needs a relation; non- insured reporters need a phone
After the claim row exists, only RC >= 90 from a sub-service fails FNOL; lesser failures are warnings
Claim opens in state OPEN on the business date after segmentation and assignment
Optimistic locking on VERSION_NO for update, close and reopen
Loss type is fixed after FNOL; changing loss date re-verifies the policy
Litigation flag cannot be cleared while a matter is open
Coverage question can be cleared only on a verified policy
Close reasons COMPLETE DUPLICAT DENIED WITHDRAW NOPAY
Close needs all exposures closed, no open/pending reserve, no pending txns or checks, no OPEN mandatory activity or matter
DUPLICAT / WITHDRAW / NOPAY only when nothing has been paid
Closing skips the remaining non- mandatory activities and frees the adjuster's capacity
Reopen only from CLSD with a reason; REOPEN_COUNT + 1
Reopen returns to the previous adjuster if active, else the assignment rules decide

programs.purpose: Claim service - first notice of loss and the claim life cycle. FNOL verifies the policy against GenApp, snapshots policy, coverages and risk units, creates the insured and reporter contacts, flags duplicates and catastrophes, segments, assigns and opens the claim with its initial activities. Also inquiry, maintenance with field-level history, close and reopen.

rules.text: Type PERS needs a last name, COMP needs a company name
Date of birth must be valid and not after the business date
Postcode required for companies and with an address; when given it must start with a letter
E-mail must contain one '@' with a '.' in the domain
A GenApp customer already held is reused (match on customer number)
Person dedupe: last name + postcode + date of birth (first name when DOB is not given)
Company dedupe: company name + postcode
New and renamed contacts are sanctions screened immediately
Contacts mirrored from GenApp are mastered there: name and DOB are read-only in claims
Roles: INSURED CLAIMANT REPORTER WITNESS ATTORNEY VENDOR DOCTOR ADVERSE
Only one INSURED per claim
A vendor must carry a vendor type
Closed claims cannot gain new parties
Sanctions match = upper-case name with spaces removed, either name order -> HIT, else CLER
A HIT writes a history row on every claim the contact is on and returns warning SANCHIT

programs.purpose: Contact (address book) service. Creates people and companies with duplicate detection, reads and maintains them, links them to claims in a role, and screens names against the sanctions list held in code table SANCTION.

rules.text: Type must be valid; BR-CLM-DOC-008 name default
Recipient must be a contact on the claim
One outstanding request per type and recipient
Requests cannot be raised on a closed claim
A DMS reference is mandatory on receipt
Only a requested (RQST) document can be received; unsolicited documents are registered as RCVD
Receiving a police report removes the NOPOLREF SIU score, lowers the claim SIU score and records history
Document name defaults to the type description

programs.purpose: Claim document requests. Requests a document from a claim contact, records receipt against a document management (DMS) reference and lists the claim's documents. Receipt of a police report withdraws the SIU "no police reference" indicator.

rules.text: Exposures are added, changed and reopened only on OPEN claims
Exposure type must fit the coverage type (VEHDAMAG COLL/COMP, BODINJUR LIAB_BI, PROPDAMA LIAB_PD/DWELLING/BLDG, CONTENTS CONTENTS, LOSSOFUS COLL/COMP/ BUSINT, MEDPAY MEDPAY)
Incident must be on the same claim and of a type that fits the exposure type
First-party coverage must cover the damaged risk unit of the incident
Injury exposures: the claimant is the injured person on the incident
One live exposure per claimant, type and coverage on a claim
Exposure sequence is the next number within the claim
New exposures open with zero reserve lines for claim cost (CLMC) and adjusting expense (EXAO)
Validation level NEWL becomes ABLE (ability to pay) when claimant, coverage and incident are present
Assignment failure leaves the claim owner as handler (warning)
Coverage cannot change once any financial transaction exists
With payments made the exposure cannot drop below ABLE
Close needs zero open and pending reserve and no transaction pending approval
Close reason PAYCMPLT needs at least one payment
Updates carry VERSION_NO (optimistic lock)

programs.purpose: Exposure service. An exposure is one claimant's loss against one policy coverage on a claim and is the level at which reserves and payments are held. Creates exposures with zero reserve lines, links the claimant, assigns the handler and raises the opening activities; maintains, closes and reopens them.

rules.text: Action R, P, A or J
Claim number and exposure seq (1-999) required for R and P
Cost type CLMC/EXAO/EXDC; category optional (DEFAULT), else COSTCAT
Amount: up to 999,999,999.99, 2 decimals; reserve >= 0, payment > 0
Fields of other actions must be blank (no stray payee on reserve)
Claim not closed; exposure exists and is not closed
Payment above the exposure's open reserve is warned before posting
Payment: payee required; type PART/FINL/SUPP (default PART), method CHEQ/BACS/FAST (default CHEQ); scheduled date today to today+30, default today
Only a txn pending approval can be decided
Approver other than the named one is warned (service checks limit)
Reject needs a reason; approve must not have one
A posted entry is never posted twice from the same screen
Post only exactly what was validated
Pending approval names the approver
Service RC >= 90 backs out the unit of work

programs.purpose: Reserve and payment entry with a confirm step, and supervisor approval / rejection of pending transactions. ENTER validates and resolves the claim/exposure (CLMCLAIM CLMINQ) or the pending txn (CLMFINTX TXNINQ) and asks for PF5. PF5 posts: R -> RSVSET, P -> PAYCRT, A -> TXNAPR, J -> TXNREJ, and shows the txn status (SUBM, or PAPR with approver) and the reserve line balances. PF12 back to entry; PF3 menu; CLEAR restart.

rules.text: Reserves and payments need an OPEN claim and an OPEN exposure
Cost types CLMC EXAO EXDC; blank category is DEFAULT, others must be in code table COSTCAT
A reserve cannot be set negative
One pending reserve change per reserve line at a time
A claim-cost reserve cannot exceed the coverage limit not yet paid
Reserve decreases need no authority; increases are checked against RSVEXP (exposure reserve) and INCCLM (claim incurred)
Over authority the transaction is PAPR with an APPRPAY activity for the first approver who covers every failed limit; with no such approver it is refused (RC 20)
Payment types PART FINL SUPP, methods CHEQ BACS FAST; amount > 0
Scheduled date not before the business date, at most 90 days ahead, rolled to a business day
Payee must exist; an unchecked payee is sanctions screened and a HIT blocks the payment
Deductible is applied once per exposure on claim-cost payments: the payment is reduced by the deductible not yet applied and a payment within it is rejected
Claim-cost payments cannot exceed the coverage limit less paid and pending payments on that coverage
SUPP payments follow a posted FINL payment and do not erode reserve
An eroding payment larger than the open reserve first raises the reserve with a linked RSV txn
A FINL payment zeroes the line's remaining reserve (linked RSV txn)
Payment authority: PAYEXP on the payment, PAYCLM on claim paid to date including the payment
Recovery categories SUBRO SALVAGE DEDUCT OVERPAY; allowed on OPEN or CLSD exposures of an OPEN claim
A receipt reduces the recovery reserve, never below zero
OVERPAY recovery is limited to net paid on the line; DEDUCT recovery to the deductible not withheld
The approver cannot be the creator and must hold the authority at the moment of approval
Only posted PAY and RCV can be voided; a payment only while its check is not ISSU or CLRD
